<think>
The problem is narrowly scoped: a single read-only GET /time endpoint on the api_test service, returning JSON with exactly two fields — "time" as the current server time in ISO-8601 UTC, and "service" fixed to the literal string "api_test". No database, no persistence, no auth changes, no state.

Decomposition: a scope this small warrants one epic (server time reporting), one feature (the GET /time endpoint itself), and a minimal task set. The natural split is (1) implement and register the endpoint handler, and (2) automated tests that pin the contract. Anything more would be over-decomposition for a read-only, no-database endpoint.

Acceptance criteria must be objectively verifiable: HTTP 200 with application/json; the body carries exactly the two named fields; "time" parses as ISO-8601 and carries a UTC designator ("Z" or "+00:00"); "service" equals "api_test" exactly; the request path touches no database. The read-only/no-database constraint is testable by asserting the handler has no persistence dependency. Complexity is low throughout; the tests task depends on the implementation task. Out of scope: timezone parameters, non-UTC formats, caching headers, and any persistence.
</think>
